name: price_channel_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Donchian Channel breakout using a 30-bar lookback on 1-min data captures new 30-minute highs/lows as trend continuation signals. When price breaks above the highest high of the last 30 bars, it has exceeded a natural resistance level and momentum traders pile in. The original Turtle Trading system used Donchian channels on daily bars; adapting to 1-min bars with a volume confirmation filter captures intraday breakout dynamics. The edge exists because genuine breakouts from 30-minute consolidations often lead to continuation due to stop-loss triggering above the old high and new momentum buying. The filtering of false breakouts via volume (>1.5x average) and VWAP alignment provides edge over naive channel breakout implementations.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

conditions: DC_width_pct > 0.3 (sufficient range to break out from)
long.confirmation: breakout bar closes within top 25% of its range: (close - low) / (high - low) > 0.75

short.confirmation: breakout bar closes within bottom 25% of its range: (close - low) / (high - low) < 0.25

entry.entry_price: market order on breakout bar close

exit.target: DC_width_pct projected from breakout point (measured move: breakout_price + DC_width)
exit.stop_loss: DC_mid (midline of the channel — if price pulls back to middle, breakout failed)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at half-channel width once profit exceeds DC_width * 0.5
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes back inside the channel (below DC_upper for longs)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; adjust size inversely with DC_width to normalize risk

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX > 14 (need some volatility for breakouts to work); < 30
filters.trend_filter: VWAP direction should align with breakout direction
filters.event_filter: skip on budget/RBI day (breakouts may reverse on macro)
other_filters: DC_width_pct must be between 0.3% and 2.0% (too narrow = noise, too wide = range too large)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — Donchian breakout is classic and well-known but volume + close position filters add edge

weaknesses: Low win rate (~40%) is psychologically difficult; many false breakouts, especially in range-bound markets
On 1-min bars, a 30-bar channel is only 30 minutes — breakout significance is lower than daily Donchian channels
Volume spike requirement may cause late entries — by the time volume confirms, the best entry price is gone
prior_art: Donchian Channel breakout is the foundation of the Turtle Trading system (Curtis Faith, 'Way of the Turtle'). Richard Donchian developed the original 20-day channel breakout in the 1960s. Adapted to intraday with shorter lookback and volume filter. Similar to 'London Breakout' strategies in FX adapted for Indian equity hours.
notes: Edge math: 0.40 * 65bps - 0.60 * 27bps = 26 - 16.2 = 9.8 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -1.2 bps. Marginally negative. Trailing stop is crucial — capturing a few outsized winners (100+ bps) pulls avg winner up. With trailing stop, avg winner may rise to 80bps: 0.40*80 - 0.60*27 = 32 - 16.2 = 15.8 bps gross, net ~5 bps. Strategy viability depends on trailing stop execution quality.
